plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy regardless of other bidders' strategies. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid (not my own bid), so bidding exactly my value ensures I only win when profitable (value ≥ price paid) and maximizes expected profit. Bidding higher risks paying more than my value if the second-highest bid exceeds my true value; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I will bid exactly $21, my true value.

This is a second-price auction, where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy. Since payment equals the second-highest bid (not my own bid), bidding exactly my value ensures I win whenever profitable (value > second-highest bid) and never overpay. Bidding higher risks paying more than my value if I win with a smaller margin; bidding lower risks losing profitable auctions. With no prior history to adjust for, truthful bidding remains optimal.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (Vickrey auction), where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so bidding above my value only risks negative profit, and bidding below my value only risks losing profitable opportunities. With no prior history to inform beliefs about opponents' strategies, and since truthful bidding is weakly dominant in this format, I will bid exactly my value of $13.
